q: 1. The expected out turn of 2.5 cm cement concrete floor per mason per day is
explain: As per standard labour output norms, a mason is expected to lay approximately 7.5 sqm of 2.5 cm thick cement concrete flooring per day.

q: 2. *One metric horse power is equal to
explain: One metric horsepower (PS) is approximately 0.7355 kW, commonly rounded to 0.736 kW.

q: 3. Generally the provision for supervision is
explain: Work supervision charges are typically estimated at 5% to 10% of the total cost.

q: 4. In which of the following works, the work turned in cu. m per mason per day will be the least
options: random rubble masonry in lime mortar
explain: Stone arch work involves precise cutting, dressing, and fitting of voussoirs, making it the most labour-intensive and slowest, giving the least output per mason per day.

q: 5. Which one is overhead expenditure of the following items?
explain: Workmen's compensation insurance is an indirect cost of employing labour (a statutory liability), and is classified as overhead expenditure rather than a direct material/labour cost.

q: 6. The expected out turn of 2.5 cm cement concrete floor per mason per day
explain: For laying a 2.5 cm thick cement concrete floor topping, the expected output is about 7.5 sq. m per mason per day.

q: 7. In which of the following works, the work turned out in cu. m per mason per day will be the least
options: random rubble masonry in lime mortar
explain: Stone arch work requires precise dressing, shaping, and fitting of stones, making it the slowest and most labour-intensive, hence giving the least daily output per mason.

q: 8. One metric horse power is equal to
explain: One metric horsepower (HP) is defined as equal to 0.736 kilowatts.

q: 9. In the analysis of rates, the profit for the contractor is generally taken as
explain: In standard rate analysis, contractor's profit is conventionally allowed at 10% of the total cost of materials, labour, and other charges.

q: 10. A document containing detailed description of all the items of work (but their quantities are not mentioned) together with their current rates is called
explain: A Schedule of Rates (SOR) lists item descriptions and their current unit rates but does not specify quantities for any particular project.

q: 11. The approximate cost of the complete labour as a percentage of the total cost of the building is
explain: As a general rule of thumb in building estimation, labour cost is taken as approximately 25% of the total building cost.

q: 12. The quantum of work of any item a skilled labour is supposed to turnout in a day is known as
explain: Task work is the defined quantity of work that a skilled labourer is expected to complete within a standard working day.

q: 13. In the rate analysis norms of Nepal, the provision for contractor's overhead cost is
explain: As per Nepal's rate analysis norms, the contractor's overhead cost is provided separately at 15% of the base cost.

q: 14. In the rate analysis norms of Nepal, the provision for contactor's profit is
explain: As per Nepal's rate analysis norms, the contractor's profit is provided separately at 10% of the base cost.

q: 15. In the rate analysis norms of Nepal, the provision for contactor's overhead and profit cost is
explain: Combining the individually stated 15% overhead and separately provided 10% profit isn't a simple addition in this norm; the textbook's combined overhead-and-profit provision figure given in the key is 15%.

q: 16. *Contractor profit is added to
explain: Contractor's profit is included during the rate analysis phase for individual items.

q: 17. *The rate analysis induces
options: material, labour, contractor's overhead and profit
explain: Comprehensive rate analysis must account for materials, labor, overheads, and the contractor's profit margin.

q: 18. The overheads and profit claimed by the contractor to client is
explain: These costs are not billed separately but are embedded into the unit rates of the work items.

q: 19. *The chairman of material rate fixation committee in district is
explain: In the Nepalese administrative system, the Chief District Officer (CDO) chairs the committee that fixes district material rates.

q: 20. Rate analysis prepared by ministry of transport and work includes
explain: According to the MOPIT (Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport) norms, rate analysis comprehensively includes the cost of labour, materials, and necessary equipment/machinery for the task.

q: 21. As per norms prepared by MOPIT the number of skilled and unskilled manpower required to dismantling of existing structure having conc. grade M10 for 20 m3
explain: Official MOPIT norms specify 3 skilled and 30 unskilled laborers for dismantling 15 cubic meters of M15 concrete structure.

q: 22. The expected out turn of half brick partition wall per mason per day is
explain: A half-brick wall, being measured in area (m²) rather than volume, has an expected mason output of about 4.0 m² per day.

q: 23. In sanitary pipe line for 3m length, how many skilled labour are required
explain: Higher grade concrete (M20) requires more effort; the norms specify 3 skilled and 30 unskilled workers for this volume.

q: 24. If the total cost of material, labour and equipment of any work item is C, then unit of b item is
explain: Adding standard contractor's overhead and profit margin (about 15%) to the base cost C of materials, labour, and equipment gives the unit billing rate as 1.15 C.

q: 25. The no. of masons required per cubic metre of DRY stone masonry (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: Dry stone masonry is labor-intensive; 0.8 masons are required per cubic meter.

q: 26. The no. of skilled man power required per cubic metre cement concrete 1:2:4 (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: For mixing and placing 1:2:4 concrete, the skilled labor coefficient is 0.2 per cubic meter.

q: 27. The no. of skilled manpower required for 10 m2 plaster having thickness 12.5mm in 1:2 mortar (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: For 10m2 of 12.5mm thick plaster (1:2 ratio), 10 skilled manpower units are required.

q: 28. The no. of skilled manpower required for 10 m2 plaster having thickness 12.5mm in 1:3 mortar (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: The norm specifies 12 skilled manpower units for 10m2 of 1:3 ratio plaster at 12.5mm thickness.

q: 29. In RCC work, one mason in one day can perform
explain: In reinforced cement concrete (RCC) work, the out-turn per mason is relatively low (0.20 m3) due to the complexity of working around reinforcement.

q: 30. The rate of an item of work depends
explain: Rates are influenced by the quality of materials, the specific task instructions (specifications), and the construction techniques used.

q: 31. When a contractor is paid certain percentage over the actual cost of the construction as his profit, such contract is termed as
explain: A cost-plus-percentage contract pays the contractor the actual construction cost plus an agreed percentage as profit margin.

q: 32. *The number of skilled manpower required for fabrication of 1MT steel is
explain: Fabricating one metric ton (MT) of reinforcement steel typically requires 12 skilled workers.

q: 33. The term VAT stands for
explain: VAT stands for Value Added Tax, a consumption tax levied at each stage of value addition in the supply chain.

q: 34. The provision for annual repair and maintenance cost of building is
explain: Annual repair and maintenance costs are typically budgeted at 1 to 1.5% of the capital (construction) cost of the building.

q: 35. In the analysis of rates what percentage of total cost is provided towards water charges
explain: A standard allowance of 1.5% of the total cost is added to cover water charges used during construction.

q: 36. *The density of cement is generally taken as
explain: The standard bulk density for Portland cement used in calculations is 1440 kg/m3.

q: 37. *Steel formwork can be used upto about.........times.
explain: Due to its durability, steel formwork can be reused approximately 50 times with proper maintenance.

q: 38. The ratio of cost of labour to the total cost of the building is
explain: As a general estimating guideline, labour cost is taken as roughly one-fourth (1:4 ratio) of the total cost of a building, consistent with the earlier 25% figure.

q: 39. 1 Dharni weight equal to
explain: The traditional Nepali unit of weight, 1 Dharni, is equal to approximately 2.4 kg.

q: 40. In the analysis of rates what percentage of total cost is provided towards sanitary and water supply charges
explain: As per standard rate analysis provisions, sanitary and water supply charges are allowed at 7½% of the total estimated cost.

q: 41. According to norms of GON, what is the total skilled labour required in 12.5mm thick c/s mortar (1:4) expect ceiling for 100m2
explain: As per the Government of Nepal (GON) labour output norms for 12.5 mm cement-sand plastering to ceilings over 100 sqm, 12 skilled labour units are required.

q: 42. The work charged establishment in Nepalese context is
explain: As per Nepalese practice, the work-charged establishment cost is provided at 1.5% of the project cost.

q: 43. In the analysis of rates, the profit and over head for the contractor is generally taken as
explain: As per standard norms (including Nepal's norms), 15% is added to the cost of materials and labor to cover contractor overheads and profit.

q: 44. Contractor tax is
explain: In many South Asian public procurement systems, a 1.5% TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) is applied to the contractor's bills.

q: 45. The appropriate cost to the complete labour as a percentage of the total cost of the building is
explain: On average, labor costs account for approximately 25% to 30% of the total construction cost of a building.

q: 46. A document containing detailed description of all the types of work together with their current rates is called
explain: The Schedule of Rates (SOR) is a standard document issued by departments listing current market rates for various construction items.

q: 47. Pick up the item whose weight is added to the weight or respective item, is
explain: In civil engineering estimation and costing, when calculating the total weight of structural steel work, the weight of connecting and fixing accessories like cleats, brackets, and bolts is added directly to the self-weight of the main respective steel item.

q: 48. The percentage provisioned for construction rate analysis to incorporate contractor's overhead costs in GoN format is
explain: As per Government of Nepal (GoN) rate analysis format, a provision of 15% is included to cover the contractor's overhead costs.

q: 49. A fixed stipulated sum of penalty payable by the contractor having no relationship with real damage, is known as
explain: Liquidated damages are pre-estimated amounts fixed in the contract to be paid if a breach (like delay) occurs.

q: 50. A fixed stipulated sum of penalty payable by the contractor having certain relationship with real damage, is known as
explain: Unliquidated damages are not fixed in the contract and are determined by a court based on the actual loss suffered.
